title: The Yakuza's Guide to Babysitting
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Toru Kirishima, a violent enforcer known as the Demon of Sakuragi, is assigned by his boss Kazuhiko Sakuragi to look after the boss's quiet seven-year-old daughter Yaeka, whose mother has been in a coma since a car accident. As the two slowly bond, Kirishima learns patience and restraint, while a former acquaintance, Mashiro, tries to drag him back to his killer past.
life_message: Caring for a child can soften even a hardened person, and family is built through patient daily attention.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Boss assigns duties and Kirishima learns restraint.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Boss, lieutenant and subordinate ranks structure every relationship.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Traditional yakuza codes and family roles.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Focus on everyday care and emotional growth.

folkways.japan: Reflects the yakuza 'family' (ikka) structure of boss and sworn subordinates, softened into a comedic household, a familiar Japanese pop-culture pattern.

winners_losers: Kirishima and Yaeka gain a loving bond; the pull of Kirishima's killer past, voiced by Mashiro, is the threat; care and family loyalty get the sympathy.
